t: Born into a Fulani family of scholars in Gobir, Usman dan Fodio preached for years among the peasants and herders of Hausaland, criticising its rulers for taxation, enslavement and what he judged to be un-Islamic practices.

When the king of Gobir moved against his community, he and his followers withdrew to Gudu in 1804, named him Commander of the Faithful and fought a jihad that by 1808 had defeated the rulers of Gobir, Kano, Katsina and other Hausa kingdoms.

He handed the running of the new state to his son Muhammed Bello and his brother Abdullahi, and returned to teaching and writing; the Sokoto Caliphate outlasted him by almost a century, until the British conquest.
dyk: Usman dan Fodio held that women should receive the same education as men and put them in the same classrooms; several of his daughters became scholars and writers, and one of them, Nana Asmaʼu, translated some of his work into local languages.
ev: Usman is born in Maratta, in Gobir, into a Fulani family of the Toronkawa clan
He begins itinerant preaching, first in Gobir and Kebbi and later in Zamfara
A mystical vision leads him to believe he has the power to work miracles and to teach his own litany, or wird
Yunfa, the new king of Gobir and once Usman's student, revokes the autonomy of Degel and tries to have him killed
Usman and his followers leave Degel for Gudu and name him Commander of the Faithful; the jihad begins with the victory at Tabkin Kwotto
By this year Usman has defeated the rulers of Gobir, Kano, Katsina and other Hausa kingdoms
The caliphate's administration is reorganised, with Muhammed Bello and Abdullahi dan Fodio governing east and west
Usman dies in Sokoto and his son Muhammed Bello succeeds him as the second caliph

f.born: 15 December 1754 in Maratta, in Gobir; a Fulani of the Toronkawa clan, son of the scholar Muhammad Fodio and Hauwa bint Muhammad
f.role: Islamic scholar, teacher and writer; Commander of the Faithful (Amīr al-Muʾminīn), named by his followers in 1804; founder and first caliph of the Sokoto Caliphate
f.known: preaching tours in Gobir, Kebbi and Zamfara from 1774; the community at Degel; the hijra to Gudu and the jihad against Gobir; the founding of the Sokoto Caliphate; the education of women; more than a hundred books and many poems in Arabic, Fulfulde and Hausa
